title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries depleted while stuck in severe traffic congestion. At least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, were found stationary following the fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported.

This is a failure of operational planning. The system was deployed into a predictable real-world condition, major public events with known traffic consequences, without sufficient battery capacity or contingency for extended gridlock. It was not a model error or a technical malfunction of the vehicles themselves. What would have caught it: either pre-event analysis of traffic patterns and battery reserves for the Fourth of July in that location, or a constraint on deployments during foreseeable peak congestion periods.

The incident follows a separate December incident when a power outage caused Waymo vehicles to stop at non-functioning traffic lights. It is not established whether these events share a common root cause or represent independent gaps in system resilience.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations after their batteries depleted while stuck in severe traffic congestion. Video evidence showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported.

In response to the incident, Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the stranded vehicles. The company stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to meet with public and private partners to improve the situation for future events. This incident follows a December incident when a power outage caused some Waymo vehicles to stop at intersections with non-functioning traffic lights in San Francisco.
